issues.description: sign_message duplicates the same mode->bytes branching that verify_signature already encodes; the asymmetric default is a footgun.
issues.detail: verify_signature defaults unknown modes via if/elif/else to CHIP_0002 tree-hash, while sign_message's else branch silently does the same for any unrecognized mode. Either centralize the mode->message-bytes transform in one helper used by both sign and verify, or raise on unknown modes in sign_message like verify does. Right now signers and verifiers can drift.

issues.description: Two functions named signing_mode_enum in the same module: one method on VerifySignature, one module-level function. Bad taste.
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines both VerifySignature.signing_mode_enum (property) and a top-level signing_mode_enum(request) function. Same name, different signatures, different semantics. Rename the free function (e.g. signing_mode_for_request) or fold it onto the request classes as a property. This will bite grep and the next maintainer.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum's boolean cascade is exactly the special-case soup good taste eliminates.
issues.detail: Four if/elif arms over (is_hex, safe_mode) with a fallthrough return is harder to read than a 2x2 dict lookup keyed by (is_hex, safe_mode). The current form also relies on reader knowing the unhandled (False, True) case lands on the trailing return. A table makes the mapping obvious and audit-friendly.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is a stub copied from elsewhere; says ':param request:' when there is no request parameter.
issues.detail: The function takes signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address but the docstring lists ':param request:' and ':return:' with nothing else. Either delete the placeholder docstring or write one that matches the actual signature. Lying docstrings are worse than missing ones.

issues.description: current_p2_puzzle_hash error message regression in did_wallet.
issues.detail: The old code raised 'Invalid inner DID puzzle.'; the new code raises 'Invalid DID inner puzzle.' Trivial reword that breaks any log scraping or test that matched the prior string. If there's no reason to change it, don't.

issues.description: Variable named hex_message holds non-hex bytes in two of four branches. Misleading name carried over from the old code.
issues.detail: In sign_message the result for BLS_MESSAGE_AUGMENTATION_UTF8_INPUT is utf-8 bytes, and the CHIP_0002 branch is a tree hash. Calling the variable hex_message is a lie inherited from the pre-refactor code. Since the refactor is touching this exact block, rename to message_bytes or message_to_sign now while it's in your hands.

review.summary: The refactor is the right shape: pulling sign/verify out of three wallet classes into a util is a real reduction. But the diff doesn't go far enough — it duplicates the mode->bytes transform between sign_message and verify_signature instead of sharing one helper, which is exactly the kind of drift this refactor was supposed to kill. wallet_request_types.py introduces two different things both named signing_mode_enum in the same file, which is sloppy. The boolean cascade for is_hex/safe_mode is a textbook good-taste cleanup (use a 2x2 table). A stub docstring and a regressed error string need trivial fixes. NEEDS-WORK — none of this is hard, but ship the refactor with the duplication actually removed.
